lead: A game remembers your best score after you close it. SharedPreferences is the Android class behind that small memory: a private key-value store for a few settings. Each setting is a key, a String name, and a value of a simple type. Android saves the pairs as one XML file inside your app's private folder. You use it for flags, scores, the last selected tab and small choices, not for lists or photos.
prereq: You need: Unit 2 for activities and the activity life cycle, because the right moment to save is onPause or onStop.

blocks.text: A key-value store keeps pairs: a key names a value. In SharedPreferences the key is a String, and the value is a String, int, boolean, long or float, or a Set of Strings through putStringSet. Android writes the pairs into one XML file under your app's private data folder. With normal permissions, other apps cannot read that file.
Use preferences for sound on/off, best score, last selected tab, or a user's language choice. Do not use them for lists, images or logs; those belong to file storage or SQLite.

head: Call
What it gives
rows: A named file, settings.xml, shared by the whole app
A file tied to one Activity, useful for one screen only
The default file for the whole app

blocks.text: MODE_PRIVATE means only your app can read the file. The older modes MODE_WORLD_READABLE and MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE are deprecated and insecure. Preferences are not encrypted, so never store a password or a bank token in plain preferences.
To write, get an Editor from the preferences object, call typed put methods, then save. To read, call a typed get method with the same key and a default value.

items: Get the file: SharedPreferences prefs = getSharedPreferences("settings", MODE_PRIVATE);
Read back: int score = prefs.getInt("best_score", 0); and boolean sound = prefs.getBoolean("sound_on", true);

blocks.text: apply() saves in the background and returns nothing. commit() saves immediately and returns true or false. Use apply() on the UI thread. Remove one key with remove("key"); remove all keys with clear().

The default is returned only when the key is missing. If you wrote an int and read it with getString, you get a ClassCastException, not the default. A listener, OnSharedPreferenceChangeListener, runs when a key changes; register it where you need live updates and unregister it when the screen goes away.

sections.h3: When to save and what to expect

blocks.text: Save in onPause() or onStop(), not only in onCreate(). Android may kill your process after it leaves the screen. Read saved values early, in onCreate() or onStart(), so the screen opens with the old choice.
Preferences suit a few dozen small values. For a thousand scores, use a database; for an image, use a file. Showing the loaded value on screen is data binding to views.
On disk the file lives at /data/data/<package>/shared_prefs/settings.xml. It is a simple XML file; the next section shows its contents for the game example.

figure.caption: putInt and putBoolean write best_score = 4200 and sound_on = false, and apply() saves them into settings.xml. After a restart, getInt and getBoolean with the same keys read 4200 and false back.

spec.aria: Three steps: a write box with putInt, putBoolean and apply; the settings.xml file holding the int 4200 and the boolean false; a read box with getInt and getBoolean returning 4200 and false.

examples.question: A game settings screen saves a best score of 4200 under the key best_score and a mute flag of false under the key sound_on, into the file settings.xml. Write the code to save both values and the code to read them back after the app restarts. State what the XML file contains.
steps: Open the named file: SharedPreferences prefs = getSharedPreferences("settings", MODE_PRIVATE);. The file path is /data/data/<package>/shared_prefs/settings.xml.
Save without blocking the UI: editor.apply();. If the question demands an immediate true or false result, use commit().
After restart, read with the same keys: int score = prefs.getInt("best_score", 0); gives 4200, and boolean sound = prefs.getBoolean("sound_on", true); gives false.
The XML file holds <int name="best_score" value="4200" /> and <boolean name="sound_on" value="false" />.
examples.answer: The code saves 4200 under best_score and false under sound_on, reads them back as 4200 and false, and settings.xml stores the int 4200 and the boolean false.

traps: apply() saves in the background and returns nothing; commit() saves immediately and returns true or false. Writing commit() when the question says 'without blocking the UI' loses marks.
Reading an int key with getString throws a ClassCastException. The type is fixed at write time, so the default is not used for a type mismatch.
getPreferences(MODE_PRIVATE) is tied to one Activity. For a setting shared by the whole app, use getSharedPreferences(name, MODE_PRIVATE) or PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferences.
MODE_WORLD_READABLE and MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE are deprecated and unsafe. Preferences are also not encrypted, so storing a password there is a security mistake.
Saving only in onCreate() misses changes made during the screen's life. Save in onPause() or onStop(), before Android can kill the process.

quiz.a: A private key-value store for simple app settings, saved by Android as one XML file under the app's data folder.

quiz.q: Name any four types you can put into SharedPreferences.
quiz.a: String, int, boolean, long and float are the five simple types; a Set of Strings (putStringSet) is the one collection allowed.
0 is the default. It is returned when the key best_score is missing from the file. If the key exists with a non-int type, a ClassCastException occurs instead.

quiz.q: Write code to save highScore 4200 and muted true into a file named game, without blocking the UI.
quiz.a: SharedPreferences p = getSharedPreferences("game", MODE_PRIVATE); SharedPreferences.Editor e = p.edit(); e.putInt("highScore", 4200); e.putBoolean("muted", true); e.apply();

quiz.q: A file stores best_score as 4200. Write code to read it with default 0 and read sound_on with default true.
quiz.a: int score = prefs.getInt("best_score", 0); boolean sound = prefs.getBoolean("sound_on", true); score is 4200; sound uses true if the key is missing.

quiz.q: A teammate saves a password and a list of 1000 scores in SharedPreferences. Explain two problems.
quiz.a: Preferences are not encrypted, so the password is readable on a rooted or backed-up device. A 1000-item list is large for an XML key-value file; a database such as SQLite is the right store.

quiz.q: A screen shows live preference values. Where do you register and unregister OnSharedPreferenceChangeListener, and why?
quiz.a: Register in onStart() or onResume() and unregister in onStop() or onPause(). This keeps the listener active only while the screen is visible and avoids leaks and updates to a dead UI.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern Android often replaces SharedPreferences with Jetpack DataStore, which avoids blocking work on the UI thread and reports errors through coroutines or flows. For secrets, EncryptedSharedPreferences once wrapped the same key-value idea with encryption, but its library is now deprecated; keys belong in the Android Keystore. Search for DataStore Preferences and Android Keystore to see the newer APIs.
